polished.title: In This Town — Bingo (60s)
polished.logline: Everybody Grandad's age parties every night. Grandad (74) stays home and trains for bingo, a game of pure luck, like it's the Olympics. At the Wednesday Bingo Final he dabs all 80 cards, the table, the pigeon and the mayor before the first number is even called. He earns a Top 10 respect ranking (the mayor removes his hat, then his hair), gets banned for life by a pigeon in a hat, and leaves the mayor a Dalmatian. So now he spends Wednesdays crowd-surfing.
polished.narrator: GRANDAD narrates in first person (cast id 'grandad': green cardigan, white grandpa hair, glasses, mustache, scale 0.97). He uses the same young, deadpan, sing-songy 'jinxy' narrator voice as ep1 (same TTS voice and youth processing). A kid's voice coming out of a 74-year-old is part of the joke, and two tags sell it in the first 3 seconds: 'AVERAGE AGE: 81' over the partying crowd, then 'ME (74)' on 'Except me.' In this episode speaker 'me' = grandad, so every 'me' HUSS beat is Grandad.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: In this town, everybody my age goes out partying.
beats.visual: Town at party_night. Crane down from street.camHigh toward street.crowdA. All 18 extras are restyled as SENIORS with a seniorSpecs() override: hair 'grandpa' #e8e8e8 or 'bald', 'cardigan'/'dress' tops in the usual bright colours, glasses/beard/mustache mixed in, and EVERYONE in a partyHat. They dance and dance2 under the string lights. One granny (hair 'bun' #e8e8e8, dress, glasses) crowd-surfs across the background on raised hands (crowdSurf). On-screen tag over the crowd: 'AVERAGE AGE: 81'.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Except me.
beats.visual: Hard cut to the outside of myHouse.window: slow push-in on the lit upstairs window, party lights flickering on the glass. Cut inside: buildRoom variant 'grandad', window 'party', lighting 'night'. Grandad sits at the desk (sit) and turns only his head to the lens (headYaw), neutral face. Name tag pops in beside him: 'ME (74)'.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Same room, room.camClose. Grandad does sitSlam with params.hits on each HUSS, slamming a chunky red bingo dabber onto a bingo card on the desk, huss face. Every hit fires makeImpactBurst and leaves a fat BLACK ink dot on the card. Small camera kick per hit. Tag with an arrow: 'BINGO DABBER'.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Gerald's ninety-one. DJ name: Hip Replacement.
beats.visual: Foam street, foam 0.6, party_night, foam.cam. 'Gerald' (senior extra: beard, sunglasses, headphones round his neck, partyHat, cardigan) arm-pumps (dance2) behind simple DJ decks next to the existing speaker. Seniors bounce waist-deep in foam around him. Tag: 'DJ HIP REPLACEMENT (91)'.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: While they're out partying, by the way, I train for bingo.
beats.visual: Back in Grandad's room, room.cam. He sits at the desk (sitIdle) beside a tall stack of bingo cards, dabber in his right hand on the desk, determined face, staring dead into the lens. Party lights strobe in the window behind him. He never looks at them.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: "A spoon is just a bowl that believes in itself." — a fork, jealous.
beats.visual: Insert on Grandad's desk under the lamp: a spoon prop and a fork prop stand upright side by side, and the fork slowly leans away from the spoon. QUOTE CARD drops in out of nowhere: cream card, big serif quote, small italic attribution. The music dips under the card.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: I count to ninety. In random order.
beats.visual: Room, lighting 'dawn', window 'sunrise' (the window shows the time of day, so no clock is needed). Grandad sits on the edge of the bed (room.bed, sit) in the think pose with the 'sleepy' face (eyes closed), meditating. Random numbers pop in and out around his head as on-screen text: '47… 3… 88… 12… 61…'. Tag: '5:00 AM'.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Training montage, one cut per HUSS (~0.22 s each). (1) Grandad stands at the desk and slams (standing) onto a card: huss face, impact burst. (2) The stack of finished cards is now taller than he is; he slams the top card, sweat face. (3) Outside on the windowsill, the pigeon in a tiny partyHat salutes with one wing (flap held at the top).

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: The cat napped on my card. He's a Dalmatian now.
beats.visual: Locked medium close-up on the desk. The cat sits in 'stare', its orange body covered in about 20 big BLACK dot decals (large enough to read at phone size), staring dead into the lens. Tag: 'DALMATIAN (now)'.

beats.speaker: cat
beats.text: Hiss.
beats.visual: Same locked shot. The cat does not move. Its mouth opens a tiny bit and a 'HISS.' caption appears. Hold one beat of silence. The mayor will repeat this framing and timing exactly later.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: "Never trust a pigeon in a hat." — a pigeon in a hat.
beats.visual: The pigeon sits on Grandad's windowsill outside the glass (room.window), still in its tiny partyHat, staring in at him: idle, then a slow head tilt. QUOTE CARD drops in.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then came the Bingo Final.
beats.visual: Town square, lighting dusk, square.cam1. The banner now reads 'SUMMER PARTY BINGO FINAL'. Bunting and balloons are up. Bleachers (square.standA/standB rows) are packed with seniors and party extras in party hats. On stage: a bingo cage on a stand and a mic stand. Tag: 'WEDNESDAY' (sets up the ending).

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Eighty cards. Even the pigeon laughed.
beats.visual: Grandad is already seated at square.chairA. The whole long table is covered in a pre-laid 8 x 10 grid of bingo cards, so nobody has to carry them. Tag: '80 CARDS'. The bleachers laugh (laugh pose) and the heckler points. Quick cut: the pigeon in its party hat, perched on the end of the table, flaps with a laugh face.

beats.speaker: mayor
beats.text: First number...
beats.visual: The mayor at the mic stand, one hand inside the bingo cage, smug face, mouth open mid-word (gold-outline mayor caption). Reverse shot: Grandad holds a dabber in his right hand and a spare in his left, determined face.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Three cuts, two hits each (sitSlam params.hits, right arm only; the left hand just holds the spare dabber). CUT 1 (hits 1-2): over the cards, huss face. Impact bursts ripple down the table, and the dot layers fill 40 cards per hit until all 80 are black-dotted. CUT 2 (hits 3-4): he dabs the bare wooden table (black dot on the wood), then the pigeon (one black dot on its chest; the pigeon makes its 'shocked' face). CUT 3 (hits 5-6): the mayor has leaned in to inspect (peer pose, which puts his face at table height). The camera is behind the mayor's head as the dabber slams down twice where his face is (impact bursts). His face is NOT shown, and his other hand is still in the cage.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Eighty bingos. Zero numbers.
beats.visual: Wide, square.cam2. The music cuts out. Every square on every card is dotted. Grandad sits back with a smug face and blows on his dabber tip like a gunslinger. The mayor has straightened up with his back to camera, frozen, ball never drawn. The crowd is stunned (stunned pose) and the heckler's party hat slowly tilts over. On-screen counter: 'BINGOS: 80 · NUMBERS CALLED: 0'.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: "Silence is applause on airplane mode." — my hearing aid.
beats.visual: QUOTE CARD over the dead-silent bleachers. Insert: Grandad taps a tiny beige hearing aid at his ear (think pose). On the word 'aid' the whole crowd erupts (cheer) and confetti bursts over the stage (makeConfetti).

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Top ten respectful moments. Number seven: the mayor removed his hat.
beats.visual: A RANKING CARD slides in: 'TOP 10 RESPECTFUL MOMENTS — #7'. The mayor is shot from 3/4 behind so his face stays hidden. He lifts off his top hat (topHat accessory off, hat prop in his right hand) and holds it to his chest (clap pose frozen with the hands together at chest height). The crowd goes reverently quiet.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Number one: his hair.
beats.visual: The card flips to '#1'. Same angle: the mayor lifts off his hair too (cut to mayor spec hair 'bald'; a brown toupee prop appears in his left hand) and holds hat and toupee together at his chest. His bald dome gleams in the dusk light. Hold one dead-serious beat.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Banned for life.
beats.visual: Close on the table. The pigeon (party hat, one black dot on its chest) glares at Grandad and does its 'huss' action (chest puffs, beak wide open) as a red rubber-stamp graphic 'BANNED FOR LIFE' slams onto the screen. Grandad shrugs with a smug face. This pays off 'never trust a pigeon in a hat': the pigeon laughed at him, then banned him.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: The mayor? Dalmatian now.
beats.visual: The mayor slowly turns to camera, bald, hat and toupee still held to his chest. His whole face and head are covered in about 15 big black dots (black on pale skin reads as a real Dalmatian at phone size). Tag: 'DALMATIAN (now)', in exactly the same style as the cat's tag.

beats.speaker: mayor
beats.text: Hiss.
beats.visual: Exactly the same framing and timing as the cat's hiss: a dead stare into the lens, the mouth opens a tiny bit, 'HISS.' caption. Hold.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Now I crowd-surf on Wednesdays.
beats.visual: Street at party_night with the string lights on. Grandad, in a party hat, crowd-surfs on the seniors' raised hands (crowdSurf) with a dabber in each fist and a calm, smug face. Tag: 'WEDNESDAY', which pays off the Bingo Final tag: bingo night is free now. Easter egg for returning viewers: this is the origin of ep1's 'My grandad crowd-surfs on Wednesdays'.

beats.speaker: town
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The crowd bounces Grandad up on each HUSS, and each time he slams a dabber onto a party hat below him (a black dot appears on the hat). Party lights pulse on every hit. Huss face. He can't stop dabbing.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Bingo.
beats.visual: Mid-surf, Grandad turns his head to the lens with a wink face, reaches toward the camera and DABS IT. A black ink dot blooms from the centre of frame until it fills the whole screen, and that is the cut to black. The viewer is the last square.

polished.whyItsFunny:
THE ENGINE: Bingo is pure luck, so a 74-year-old grinding for it at full HUSS intensity is already absurd. Each training beat pushes 'luck as a skill' one step further: counting to ninety in random order, then a cat turned 'Dalmatian' that only says 'Hiss.' (the user's literal 'hiss'). The two tags 'AVERAGE AGE: 81' and 'ME (74)' sell the kid's voice coming out of a mustached grandad within 3 seconds, so it plays as a joke, not confusion.

FIXES TO THE JUDGES' NOTES:
- 'Legs eleven' is gone. It is replaced by the mayor saying 'First number...', which anyone understands. The joke is that Grandad finishes before the number exists.
- 'Eighty bingos. One number.' becomes 'Eighty bingos. Zero numbers.' The frenzy SHOWS how: every card, then the table, then the pigeon, then the mayor's face. So the counter, the ban and the reveal all explain themselves, and the impossibility now reads as the punchline.
- The frenzy escalates (cards, table, pigeon, mayor), so it is more visual than ep1's chess slam. The ending adds crowd-surf dabbing and a fourth-wall lens dab.
- Top 10 is now a visual laugh: #7 the mayor removes his hat (normal respect), #1 he removes his HAIR. A bald dome and a toupee held to his chest in dead-serious silence.
- No 'dab' dance pun. Dabbing is only the literal bingo tool.
- Dots are BLACK. The cat's dots read even with the tag, and on the mayor's pale skin they genuinely look like a Dalmatian.
- The weakest quote (birth certificate) is replaced by the judges' favourite line, 'A spoon is just a bowl that believes in itself' — a fork, jealous (grafted from pitch 1). The silence quote is rewritten as 'applause on airplane mode', which teens recognise and which avoids repeating the 'X is just Y' shape.
- The ending works without ep1. The biggest laugh is a callback inside this episode: the mayor turns to camera covered in dots, 'The mayor? Dalmatian now.', then he says 'Hiss.' in exactly the cat's framing. The 'WEDNESDAY' tag planted at the Bingo Final pays off when the ban frees up his Wednesdays, and 'Except me' flips to him finally being the one at the party. 'Bingo.' as he dabs the lens is the button: the viewer is the last square. For returning viewers, it is also the origin of 'My grandad crowd-surfs on Wednesdays'.
- 'Never trust a pigeon in a hat' pays off without words: the same pigeon in a hat laughs at him, gets dabbed, then puffs up as the ban stamp lands.

TIMING: 126 spoken words, 4 huss beats, 18 HUSSes. Measured on ep1's real timeline, a 6-HUSS takes 1.64 s and a 3-HUSS 0.66 s, so the HUSSes total about 4.6 s. Ep1 fit 127 words, 27 HUSSes (6.9 s) and 27 beats into 60.2 s. This script has 9 fewer HUSSes and 2 fewer beats, which leaves about 2-3 s for the three quote-card holds and the two 'Hiss.' holds, so it lands around 58-60 s.

PRODUCTION NOTES:
- Right arm only (sitSlam/slam with params.hits); the second dabber is just held, so no mirrored left-arm slam is needed.
- No carry: the 80 cards are pre-laid on the table.
- No clock through the window: window 'sunrise' plus a '5:00 AM' tag.
- No flying glasses.
- The mayor's face stays hidden (shot from behind or 3/4 behind) from the frenzy until the reveal. 'Peer' puts his face at table height so the downward slam works.
- Hat to chest is the 'clap' pose frozen.
- The toupee is a spec hair swap to 'bald' on a cut plus a prop.
- One seniorSpecs() override covers the street, foam and square sets.
- Montage: 3 inserts of about 0.22 s. Frenzy: 3 cuts with 2 hits each.

pitches.whyItsFunny: The base joke is that bingo is pure luck, so a man grinding for it at full intensity with HUSS dab-slams is already absurd. The 'grandad' room variant and the sitSlam action make it easy to film. Each training beat pushes the 'luck as a skill' logic one step further: counting to ninety in random order, then the cat turned into a 'Dalmatian' that just says 'Hiss.' (a nod to the 'hiss' in the request). The payoff is a feat that can't happen, eighty bingos off one number. The 'Top ten respectful moments' bit has an extra layer. The mayor's hat removal ranks only #7, and #1 goes to the same pigeon that laughed at him, which also quietly answers the earlier quote 'Never trust a pigeon in a hat' (no hat, so now you can trust it). The three quotes drop in at random but still fit loosely: an old man who skips parties, the pigeon in a hat, and a silent crowd. The single red dot planted on the mayor's forehead pays off in the twist: banned for life for dabbing the mayor. The final line reveals the backstory behind ep1's throwaway line 'My grandad crowd-surfs on Wednesdays', so it pays off for returning viewers. pitches.whyItsFunny: 1) The opener hides a reveal. "Everybody parties. Even the pigeons. ... Except me." Then the camera lands on a pigeon, so the narrator turns out to be the pigeon. 2) It's a bird's-eye version of the format. The most pointless thing a pigeon could grind is a political campaign. The catchphrase also does real story work: "While they're out partying, by the way, I'm knocking on their doors" is exactly why 400 doors never open. 3) The setup pays off cleanly: "ten thousand rehearsals" becomes one flat "Coo." Then "Silence. A balloon fainted." swaps the standard "crowd went silent" for an absurd image. 4) The Top 10 bit lands as a joke, not a list. The mayor giving up his hat is only #7, and "Numbers one to six? Also me." flips through polaroids of the pigeon doing nothing. The hat swallowing him whole is a visual gag that runs to the end. 5) It calls back to ep1 several times: the town threw "a birthday party for the mayor's pigeon", the mayor, the cat (who now votes for himself), and the pigeon who "was winning". 6) The twist uses bird logic and flips the format. The grinder wins and bans parties, which kills his own food supply: no parties, no crumbs. So the closing mirrors the opening: "Now in this town, everybody grinds. Except me." He's the only one partying, with a cake for crumbs, and says "Don't tell the mayor" while he is the mayor. 7) Each quote card is a random non-sequitur that still loosely fits where it drops. A spoon "believing in itself" is the underdog campaign. The goose "under oath" fits speeches and loudness. "The moon is just a big crumb" lands on the hunger twist. The attributions (a jealous fork, a goose under oath, "me, hungry") each carry a second joke.

pitches.whyItsFunny: The skill is absurd but very simple: not blinking. That gives the grind deadpan gags that cost almost nothing to animate (out-staring a toaster, a wall that cracks first). The HUSS face is flipped from eyes squeezed to eyes wide, so even the grind sound becomes a joke. The three quotes drop in out of nowhere, and each attribution is the punchline: the fish quoting itself, Grandad saying it while asleep, and a burglar with an obvious reason to want windows open. The Top 10 bit is a reversal. The narrator builds it up as a solemn countdown, number seven is just a pigeon taking his hat off, and then numbers one to six are also the pigeon. The twist is that after a year of training she loses to one ordinary 'Say cheese!' She blinks for the first time in the one photo that matters, and the town turns it into a statue with a NEVER BLINKED plaque. The pigeon taking his hat off on the statue's head closes the episode by calling back the respect gag.

pitches.whyItsFunny: It flips the format. In a town that never stops moving, the grind is literally not moving, so every HUSS is a sweaty shout from a body that stays completely still. Freeze poses are also the easiest thing our rig can do. The training escalates from 'four seconds' to 'the cat thinks I'm a shelf' and Grandad dusting her like furniture, which is also Top-10 respectful moment #7. The final opponent being a lamppost, knocked out for 'flickering', is a dumb-perfect payoff. The 'while you were out partying, by the way' line looks like a cool mic drop. Then the ranking card comes back for #1: Marcus lifts her sunglasses, she's asleep, and the comeback was sleep-talk. That turns her signature sunglasses into a twist, and it also explains how she out-froze a lamppost. The weird quotes land as non-sequiturs that still click: fish can't blink, a moth warns you not to be a moth, a dentist tells you to be full of snacks, and the pigeon's 'hotel' line plays while it literally moves into her bun. The last button is that her snore is a HUSS, so she is still grinding in her sleep.

judgements.reasoning:
Judged as a 15-year-old scrolling TikTok: which one gets a laugh out loud and gets sent to the group chat?

The winner is Pitch 1, Pigeon for Mayor. It has the most clip-able moments.
- After ten thousand HUSS rehearsals, the whole speech is one flat "Coo." That is the biggest single laugh in any of the four pitches.
- Two visual punchlines follow it right away: "A balloon fainted" and the top hat swallowing the pigeon so only its feet stick out.
- It has the best version of the Top 10 bit. "Numbers one to six? Also me." is a joke in its own right, not just a ranking card. The spoon/fork quote is the line that would get copied into the comments.
- The pigeon was ep1's final punchline, so a pigeon narrator in the jinxy voice already feels like a fan-favourite spin-off.
- The catchphrase does work here. Door-knocking "while they're out partying" means nobody is home to answer.

The risks are real:
- It is too dense: 27 beats in 134 words, across seven locations.
- The ending ("now everybody grinds", window HUSSers) repeats ep1's ending, and the "partying alone at the end" twist is close to the cricket reference.
- The goose quote is filler.
- Fixes: cut the goose quote and "My speech:", and make the birthday motive clearer. Then it is the strongest episode.

The other three:
- **Pitch 2 (Don't Blink)** is a close second and has the tightest story with the best twist: she blinks in the photo and the statue has its eyes closed. But its Top 10 bit has nothing to do with her story. It also needs engine work: a new hero, a new face variant and a flag to switch blinking off.
- **Pitch 0 (Bingo)** has great individual lines ("DJ Hip Replacement", the Dalmatian cat, a literal "Hiss.", the lens-dab ending). But "Legs eleven" won't land with most teens, and the twist only pays off if you remember ep1.
- **Pitch 3 (Freeze Dance)** is the easiest to produce and has clever structure: the catchphrase is the punchline and the twist goes through the Top 10. But it has fewer big laughs, and a hero who never moves makes the HUSS beats visually flat.

judgements.reasoning:
Bingo wins. It has the best absurd-grind premise in the batch: Grandad trains like it's the Olympics for bingo, a game of pure luck. That is the same energy as the burger-wrapping reference, but original.

Joke density is the highest of the four. 'DJ name is Hip Replacement', 'count to ninety in random order' and 'He's a Dalmatian now' are each clippable on their own. The Dalmatian line plus 'Hiss.' also literally covers the user's 'weird stuff like hiss'.

It is also the only pitch where the required bits work together instead of sitting side by side:
- The quote 'Never trust a pigeon in a hat' sets up the pigeon who laughs at Grandad.
- That pigeon then removes its hat as Top 10 #1, so the skip from #7 to #1 lands.
- The single dab dot planted on the mayor's forehead at #7 pays off as 'Banned for life. Apparently, you can't dab the mayor.'
- The ending turns ep1's throwaway 'My grandad crowd-surfs on Wednesdays' into an origin story, which rewards returning viewers. The lens-dab 'Bingo.' button is the best final frame of the four.

It is also the cheapest to make: existing grandad room, sitSlam with synced hits for kinetic HUSSes, crowdSurf, setAccessory for the hat removals, impact bursts, and senior extras restyled with the existing grandpa hair and cardigan.

Before production, fix three things:
1. Cut one HUSS triplet so 24 HUSSes, about 129 words and the card holds fit in 60 s.
2. Show him dabbing everything, so the 80 bingos read and the ban makes sense.
3. Make the Dalmatian dots dark so they read.

Runner-up is pitch 2 (Don't Blink). It has the single best twist (the blink in the photo leads to a NEVER BLINKED statue with its eyes shut) and the most teen-relatable premise. But it is a near line-for-line ep1 template, its Top 10 bit is a disconnected pigeon gag shared with pitch 1, and it needs new character and face-system work. It's worth keeping in the bank for ep3.

Pitch 1 has great moments ('My speech: Coo.', 'A balloon fainted'). But it is overstuffed at 28 beats, the most expensive to build, and its ending repeats ep1's town-grinds finale.

Pitch 3 has the best lamppost and hotel lines. But its HUSS beats are motionless, its asleep twist undercuts the grind, and it reuses ep1's burn exchange.

judgements.reasoning:
Pitch 0 (Grandad Bingo) wins on producibility plus visual comedy, with Pitch 2 a close second. Bingo builds almost entirely on assets we already have: the grandad character and his room variant, the square with a swappable banner, the foam street and speaker, the bleacher crowd, and the ep1 grandad crowd-surf. It needs no new character, face, emblem or material system. Its HUSS beats are the best fit of the four for our engine: a dabber slammed on every HUSS is exactly what sitSlam with params.hits was built for in ep1, and every hit leaves a visible red dot. The visual jokes are physical and read at phone size: the dotted Dalmatian cat stares and goes 'Hiss.' (which also covers the user's literal word), the mayor's face is covered in dots, he crowd-surfs gripping a dabber in each fist, and he dabs the lens for a full-screen red splat. The writing plants the payoff: one dot on the mayor's forehead in the #7 card becomes a dozen in the BANNED reveal. 'You can't dab the mayor' is a double meaning teens get instantly. The ending turns ep1's throwaway 'My grandad crowd-surfs on Wednesdays' into a payoff for fans. It has every format element (5 HUSS beats, the catchphrase mid-sentence, Top 10 #7 then #1, 3 absurd quotes) at 132 words. Fixes before it ships: a mirrored left-arm slam for two-handed dabbing, a carry pose for the card tower, cutting to an exterior for the 5:00 clock, and tightening the montage.

It costs more custom work: a new hero spec plus emblem, a blink flag, a stone-material statue, render-to-texture pigeon polaroids, hug/kneel/slump poses and a lighting time-lapse. Its Top 10 is also an unrelated pigeon gag. It's the clear backup and should be the next episode.

Pitch 1 (Pigeon for Mayor) has the best single quote (the spoon) and the best catchphrase use (knocking on doors while everyone is out partying). But it copies the reference video's party-ban twist and re-runs ep1's window-grinders ending. It's also the hardest to shoot: a 0.45 m hero in a human-scale set, 28 beats, about 25 setups, and missing door anchors.

Pitch 3 (Freeze Dance) is the easiest to build, but its premise is a character standing still. That kills the HUSS energy, and her sunglasses hide the huss eyes. It also re-runs ep1's 'While you were out partying' exchange almost word for word, and its Top 10 #1 isn't a respectful moment.
